title: Understanding National Freedom, Independence & Sovereignty
paragraphs: Understanding national freedom, independence, and sovereignty. We use these words as if we know their meaning. In fact, I doubt that some of our leaders really know what it means. These are lofty words, great ideals, and tremendous aspirations, but do we truly understand the meaning of these words: freedom? Do we understand the meaning of independence? Do we understand the meaning of sovereignty? Like other nations, we are building a nation. I don't believe a nation is ever complete.

We build it, we build it, and we continue to build it. So, we are not on our way to the end, but rather we are in the process of building. I would like to address a few points, the first of which is about the foundations of nations. Write down these points. First, what is the foundation of all nations? the law. This is extremely important. Secondly, nations are built on law, and indeed, their existence continues thanks to it.

Third, the law determines the quality of life in any nation, through the people’s adherence to it, and the nobility of these laws. Fourth, the law protects national life. All communities must abide by the law. The word "society" is derived from the word "social," and relates to our relationship with each other within a group. The law regulates these relationships. Sixth, society is created and built by law. What makes any people a society is their agreement to abide by the same standards.

Society is the product of agreement, not unification. Sixth, and this is extremely important, society is created by law because laws shape the culture of that group. How important is law in building a state? Let's take another look at the priority of the law. Law is the first and most important component in nation-building. A nation was born a few days ago, and that nation is South Sudan. The first thing they had to prepare was what they call a constitution.

When the Bahamas was founded, as everyone says, the first thing we had to prepare for the colonial mother country was a document called the Constitution. The constitution is an embodiment of the aspirations, ideals, and principles of life of this group of people. This leads me to the second point: the law is the source of national cohesion. We remain united only thanks to constitutional commitment.

Therefore, the law is the fabric in which national life is woven, meaning that it is the primary source for building society. The law is also the mother that gives birth to civil society. If we talk about living in a civilized manner, there must be laws that we agree upon, such as: Do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not covet your neighbor’s property. This is what lays the foundations of civilization. Civil society must also operate in accordance with the law.

Can you imagine not receiving your salary until the end of the week? This may seem simple, but it is dangerous. You will not receive your salaries until the end of the month. Do you realize what that means? You have already done it. Let's assume they didn't pay. In other words, you need to trust that the company will fulfill its legal obligation to pay your salaries. You have already done it. Wouldn't it be great if they paid you first? I'm not sure.

Because most of you will be going straight to Florida at the beginning of the month, and may God protect us at the end of it. But we rely on the law so that we can trust each other with our energy and time. Therefore, the key to nation-building— please note this term—is constitutional law. Constitutional law, I want the young people present today, please, to listen to me for the first time with an attention you have never listened to me before. Because I rely on you to keep our country running properly.

Please study your constitution. Because if you do not understand your constitution, you will not know your rights. We must protect the law because the law is what created us. What do I mean by that? The constitution, as I mentioned, is an embodiment of the people’s aspirations, desires, and national vision. It is also the source of law, and laws originate from it.

In fact, laws are made to protect the constitution, and they are a product of the constitution, which defines your rights, and then laws are made to protect those rights. Therefore, the law is enacted to ensure that you receive fair judgments in the event that anyone attempts to violate what the constitution guarantees you. Judges are appointed to protect the law. When you enter a courtroom, the judge's role is to protect the constitution and the laws that were enacted to protect your constitutional rights.

Lawyers are guardians of the law, meaning they are tasked with enforcing it and ensuring that it is not used to violate citizens' rights. They are also supposed to represent your legal rights in court. As for the police and law enforcement agencies, their job is to enforce the law, and this is a problem in many countries. But the job of the police and any law enforcement agency is to enforce the law, not to make it. They are supposed to ensure its implementation.

And the citizens, the last group, are supposed to abide by the law. This means obeying the law. They stopped at the traffic light. Slow down at the stop sign. Let the pedestrians cross. Don't steal the paper clip from the office. Okay. Do not lie about being sick when you are not sick. This is the law. Ladies and gentlemen, it is surprising that when I reread our constitution, I decided today to review two of the most important aspects of our constitutional document.

Some of you have never read it word for word before. We have read it before. I want to review it slowly. I want to show you what Sir Lyndon Pendlegg, Milo Butler, and E. have written. D. Hannah, Cecil Wallace Whitfield, Doris Johnson, Johnston, Frances, and all the names our children don't know. The men who sacrificed their lives for the Bahamas. Those who gave their lives to establish this country. I want to read with you what they wrote as a basis for the Bahamas.

And I want you to read this carefully, please, because this is why we need to be careful about what we allow the United Nations to do. You all better pay attention. Because this is the crucial moment, right here. Here we can actually sue any government. No government is more powerful than the constitution. Listen to me, all of you. I am not speaking to anyone in particular, but to everyone. I am reading a document that we all have. Here's what the constitution begins with. Let's read it together.

The rediscovery of this group of islands, rocks and islets 481 years ago heralded the birth of the New World. This is the arrival of Columbus. So, they wrote that there. We come from a rich history. Now, this is what they wrote. the next. And since the people of this group of islands, realizing that the preservation of their freedom would be assured through a national commitment to self-discipline, hard work, loyalty, and unity, one of them said: "Let's put this in place."

I do n't know who was around that table, but one of them said: "Endless respect for Christian values ​​and the rule of law." Both statements are dangerous. Personally, I prefer the phrase "constant respect ". Respect always means: Don't touch this. It's better if you discuss it with me. Permanent respect means: no matter what anyone, man or woman, wears— striped trousers and a black coat—and enters the House of Representatives, they must not touch this thing. Respect always means: Don't touch this.

Oh my God, you are not helping me here. I am now in a critical situation. We have a member of parliament here. Everyone will be told what I will say tomorrow. Enduring respect. Everyone says: Respect. Respect means: even if you don't want to submit to him, don't touch him. If you want to live a miserable life, that's fine, but respect this standard. I'm alone here, that's okay. We don't care about your personal lifestyle, but this obliges us to respect this standard. Don't speak ill of this standard.

You may not go to church, but we will go and we will not compromise on this standard. You may be Buddhists, Muslims, Confucians, or perhaps you practice magic. Don't touch him, help me. I told you today, I will hide nothing. Respect. Respect means you don't have to like him. Please come in. I think Milo Butler probably said that at the meeting. Or perhaps it was Darris Johnson of Battle Baptist Church who said, "You'd better put that in there." Or perhaps it was Professor Dr.

Hanna, although we do not know what his commitment was at that time, at least he knew from his grandmother that it was better to trust in God. Help me, guys, I'm alone here. Come on, say Amen and peace be upon you. Enduring respect. For Christian values. Now, read the following statement. Isn't this in our constitution? Read. Now know then that we are the heirs of the lineage of the successors of this family of islands, acknowledging what? By the sovereignty of God. Stop, stop, stop. This is your constitution.

Well, you know, we don't want God in government. What? So you must leave. Guys, it's okay. Do you see? I don't want God in this house, so leave the house. God will not leave the Bahamas. Hmm? I read in your constitution, as you know. You see, you didn't know it was this obvious. Now, no one has said sovereignty. Sovereignty means that any proposal you put forward... Any idea you present on a white paper, any policy you want us to consider, must be reviewed in the light of God. That's what it means.

Sovereignty means that you do not violate it with your policies. Oh, calm down. We admit it. He didn't say that we should believe in him, as you know. Some of them do not believe in it. But that's none of your business. They acknowledged that he, not you, is the sovereign of the Bahamas. They applauded me warmly. I do n't know, but you know... sometimes when people get a taste of power, they start to feel vain. According to our constitution, no one has sovereignty in the Bahamas except God. Which god?

The Christian God. We can announce that. What do we believe in? With the fundamental rights and freedoms of the individual. Now, this is a very important statement. Because firstly, it tells you that God is sovereign. Then he says: "Now, you can have all the rights and freedoms you want afterwards." No, you didn't understand that. Let me tell you something. Miles Monroe, turn on the TV. I will go to court myself. I will sue any member of parliament who is confused.

First, Milo Butler, Selena Penelope, and John Stone said that God is sovereign. Now, you can be as free as you like and do as you please under the sovereignty of God. This means you are as free as you want, as long as you do not violate God’s law. This is important now. People are walking around, demanding human rights. Yes, human rights are granted under the sovereignty of God. You are not free to do anything. You are free to do anything he approves of. Scream. We need to be careful now.

Because they like to use this word, you know, rights. But rights must be in context. For example, you do not have the right to enter my yard and take the mangoes. I mean, you're free now. You can walk around the courtyard freely. But you do not have the right to wander around the yard. So, don't say anything to my face; every human being has the right to be free. Yes, under the sovereignty of God. There needs to be context. Yes. As you know, look at the following phrase. Read.

We proudly and honorably declare the establishment of a free, democratic, and sovereign state, founded on spiritual values. Now you will all scream. You see, you don't understand. It would be better if you said something. Aren't you clapping? Let me tell you something. I was naive, you know. I thought it was based on logic. I thought it was based on British policy and British principles.

But the drafters of our constitution said that we would establish a nation not on technical, educational, psychological, or emotional foundations, but on spiritual foundations. Wow! Do you know what this means? This means that the spiritual values ​​of every member of our government must be examined. And we know what values ​​we are talking about. Who are we talking about? It's not just about the sovereignty of God, the God of Christianity, meaning that the Bible is the standard of your spiritual values.

Please, priest. Good. Help yourself. I'm thinking about what I'm going to say. One minute, please. I have to be careful, you know. When someone knocks on your door in the next few weeks, keep a copy of this in your hands. Available online. Just download and copy it. Say: "Excuse me, sit here. I'll get you a cup of tea. Let me read this to you." Now, what are your spiritual values? Are you weak-willed? Yes, I said that. Because according to the sovereignty of the God of the Bible, we have a problem here.

That's why you have a constitution to evaluate decisions based on. Lord, help me. Help me. Help me. Help me. Lord, I am very scared today. I need some help. You all must help me. They built this on spiritual values. Don't stop here. Read the following statement.

"According to which no man, and this is important now, or woman, or child shall ever be a slave or subject to anyone, or, and this is important, have their labor exploited, or, which is of utmost importance, have their lives frustrated by the burden of their support." Let me put this in context. Look at what the constitution says.

If you decide to hold fast to a spiritual value of faith in God, it is illegal for anyone to manipulate the system to deny you your right to promotion, more money, doing business, or getting loans from banks, and they may even be imprisoned. You don't understand what I mean. Look, as soon as you start talking about certain topics, some groups will say, "We will not allow him to get a loan."

But the constitution states that if I have a certain conviction based on spiritual values, and therefore disagree with you, you cannot withhold a loan from the bank from me. I can constitutionally sue you and imprison you for deprivation and hindering my progress. Oh, you don't understand what I mean. Oh. So, you are a Christian? Hmm. You will not get a promotion at this company. Oh, really? Okay, let me hire a lawyer. Okay. Okay. Take this piece from here. File a lawsuit against them. I will go with you.

Yes, we will shut down that company and fire that CEO because he is denying you your right to hold your own beliefs about the spiritual values ​​of the Supreme God in Christianity. Is this clear enough? Some of you have been suffering for ten years because you say, "They do n't know what I believe in, so they won't give me any promotion today." This is illegal. Some people say: " If you oppose our group, they have a lot of money." Yes, I have a lot of power.

All I have to do is prove that your behavior towards me is based on my spiritual values. If that is the case, we will find you or throw you in jail. Don't give in to the status quo. So, don't threaten me. Don't deprive me. Don't discourage me. They applied for a housing loan. You may have applied for a mortgage. Perhaps you have applied for state-owned land. There are some people who hold strange values. They say, " Well, we won't allow that to happen." Oh, really? I want to know who is obstructing this.

If you smell something, we will consider you to be in violation of the constitution. Okay. I'm going home. No one has the right to enslave you. And by the way, let me tell you this too, because this point affects the United Nations. As you can see, the United Nations thinks it is a god. Secondly, she believes it is the world government. Hmm. So they sit in their luxurious halls and issue resolutions aimed at making universal human rights laws enforceable, without caring who they are talking to.

Then they say to your country: If you do not cooperate with the United Nations, we will withhold some privileges from you worldwide. But the constitution states that they have no right to thwart our constitutional independence and deprive us of anything because of our values. You all don't understand what I just said. Therefore, we can sue them based on our constitution before the International Court of Justice. We can sue the United Nations. Why?

Because they try to impose values ​​on us that deprive us of our convictions, and then they try to punish us for our belief system. This is a satanic act. It's best if you all help me, otherwise I'll be left alone. I'm going to show you something in a little while that you won't believe. But look at the following statement, don't you? This is stated in your constitution. I am reading it. Read it. Let's go. We hereby declare the indivisible unity and creation under the care of God of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas.

Under God's protection. I don't think any constitution in the world mentions God more than ours. Good. So, our constitution says that our country is under the care of God. Therefore, when I say to the world while I travel, that God lives in the Bahamas, it is true. We live under the authority of God constitutionally. Now, I want to show you something you've never heard of before. First, take your pens and write this down.

Let me list for you the twelve commitments we have made to our nation on this great day, Independence Day. We have written it down in our document. First, we say that this is a national obligation. This term is used in the preamble to our constitution. Let's all say: a national commitment. They chanted loudly: National commitment. Repeat it: My country. Do you know what this means? This means that the entire nation has agreed to abide by these matters. First, freedom.

Secondly, unwavering respect for Christian values. Third, the rule of law. This is extremely important. Fourth, the sovereignty of God. Do you know anything? I don't think we're serious about the rule of law until we have the courage to jail a preacher or a member of parliament. Did you hear what I said? Look, the rule of law means that no one is above the law. The Prime Minister does not govern the Bahamas.

The law is what governs the Bahamas, which means that if our Prime Minister, whoever he may be at any time in history, violates constitutional law, we can prosecute and imprison him. I'm sure you all know that the presidents of two countries were jailed last week for violating their countries' constitutions. They did not care whether they were prime ministers or heads of state. They were both thrown in jail last week. We will not be serious until we reach this level. Have you ever heard of this before?

I am seeking justice. Then he says: "It's just us." Look, justice is for some people, but not for everyone. This is the problem. When the law is violated, it becomes useless. This means that someone has broken the law. Ladies and gentlemen, fourthly, the sovereignty of God. Write it down. Fifth, what are we committed to? With fundamental rights and freedoms. Sixth, we are committed to free and democratic activity. Fourth, we commit to being a sovereign nation. This is a national obligation.

This means that any country that tries to rule us is illegitimate. This is the meaning of sovereignty. You cannot dictate to us what we do with our local social policies. As you know, some time ago a ship docked here carrying some people whom we were not enthusiastic about because their value system was not compatible with our national commitments. They went back and told all the radio programs that the Bahamas were such and such. Well, at least thank God they are aware of our differences. Isn't that so?

If you sell your convictions for a piece of bread, you do n't deserve to live on this planet. Eighth, we commit to basing ourselves on spiritual values. Ninth, we commit to ensuring that no one shall ever be a slave. This is still happening. We have sophisticated slavery in the Bahamas. There are certain contracts that our people cannot obtain. This is slavery. You will be amazed at what happens behind closed doors; they call you by name and say things you will never get. Slavery. Tenth, what are we committed to?

By exploiting labor. As you know, we have to keep an eye on this, because look at what we are going through after 38 years. I don't have to say anything. Use your brains. Look at items 10 and 11. What are we committed to? Never let our lives be ruined. How many of you in this room are frustrated because of your beliefs? You will not be satisfied with submitting to your manager, so the manager will refuse to promote you. You can sue him. Why? Because the constitution protects you.

You can never be discouraged because of your spiritual values ​​and beliefs. But we don't know that. Therefore, we are subject to the manager's standards. We live with guilt throughout our lives. Clause 12. We acknowledge that we are created under the care of God. Now, ladies and gentlemen, do you know why those who want to change our culture are trying to change the constitution? Look, if they can remove these clauses from the constitution, they will do whatever they want.

I am convinced, I have no proof of that, but I am convinced that anyone who tries to change the constitution is most likely someone in the government. They sit around the table. Because they have their own motives. Well, that will only happen over my dead body. I do n't know your opinion, but you know... no, no, no, no. Let me tell you this. What I am about to read to you, you have probably never seen before. What I have just finished reading is the preamble. Now, I will read you Article One of the Constitution.

Are you ready? This article is taken directly from the constitution. Let's read it. This is the first article. Number one, loudly. The Commonwealth of The Bahamas is a sovereign democratic state. I finish. This is the first article. Sovereign. This means that it doesn't matter what other bodies in the world do, or what decisions they make. First, we must check our constitution to see if we accept what they have decided. Why? Because we are sovereign. We try to be careful.

Therefore, as a leader of the country, you cannot decide to approve a decision issued by an external body without verifying whether it is consistent with our constitutional standards. That's what it means. We are sovereign. You cannot force us to accept anything. This is the meaning of sovereignty. We may accept what you know, but you cannot force us. We, as a people, have to decide that. You should all applaud here, please. No one in the government can decide what we all believe. You guys are slow, man.

I feel lonely. Let me come back here alone. Once again, alone. Let me go here alone. I am here alone. I can stay alone. I swear to God, I am here. Thank God. Now, read the following statement in the Constitution aloud. Start, number two. Article number two. This Constitution is the supreme law of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas and is subject to the provisions of this Constitution. Continue reading. If any law conflicts with this Constitution, this Constitution shall prevail. This is in your constitution.

We don't read the constitution. Members of Parliament do not read that. Do you realize how serious this statement is? This means if... read the last sentence. The other law is invalid to the extent of the conflict. Oh my God, I need lawyers to help me. Help me, lawyers, please help me. The United Nations says something, and whatever they say, it contradicts our constitution, and whatever their decision is in New York, it is invalid here on these islands. Please help me. Why do I need two sessions for this?

Because I want to show you a document. It's here on the screen, it will appear soon. You will see in it the countries that voted in favor of the resolution on gay and lesbian rights, and the countries that voted against it. What baffles me is that some of the most degenerate countries voted against it. O Lord, have mercy on us. How many of you are sitting here? A church full of people every Sunday, then they flatter people in exchange for a plate of porridge. Am I alone here?

Do you really want to see God bless our country? Let us decide to stand with God. I tell you this. Oh Lord, I wish I were Prime Minister. I'm telling you the truth. My first speech will set things right. I will put in place a plan for fifty years. It will be clear to the whole world: Do not touch those people there. Look at this statement. He says: "If any law is conflicting." Okay. Why did Milo put that? Because he knew that we would become very advanced later on. Yes.

We are so intellectually inclined in our region that we have started to say: "We need to be more liberal." He said, "Do not touch this. Do not touch this." Do not touch him. Do not touch him. You shouldn't have come here today. I want everyone to get a copy of this and print ten copies. Do you understand what I mean? Just copy it. Give it to every bohemian because people who live under pressure don't realize they're supposed to be under pressure. How strange. That's all. It is invalid.

Now, I want you to write this down quickly. First, here's what this statement says. The law is supreme. Second, the Constitution states that if any law is conflicting, whatever the law may be, and wherever its source may be, north, south, east, or west, when it reaches our shores, we must measure it according to our constitutional standards. And if it is not compatible, we are not supposed to apologize for it.

I don't understand why someone doesn't stand up in parliament, speak frankly, and say: "Ladies and gentlemen, I appreciate what you are discussing, but know from the beginning that I cannot participate in this discussion because the constitution prevents me from being here." What you are doing is contrary to my country's constitution. I'm going back to the Bahamas, and I'm going to swim and drink some swicha. Someone needs to stand up and say, "Look, we don't accept this."

Yes, but as you can see, if you do that, you won't get any money. You know, people won't give you any money for what you do. You will not receive any money. Let me tell you something. Let me tell you something. Let me say this publicly. If I discover that you are refusing to provide services to our community because we have gone against your personal decision, I will inform all our members that they should no longer deal with your bank, store, or business. I will start a revolution. We will break you.

We will break you. Look, let me tell you something. They are threatening you with money. the money? I don't tell my wife, you know, she said, you know, that she can live without me. If she goes to prison, she will be happy. I feel like Nelson Mandela today. Do you understand what I mean? It's too late for me now. Listen, you can do whatever you want to me. I will reply to you. Because we cannot sit idly by and let the place collapse, and we have a constitution to protect us.

The statement says that, according to this constitution, it shall prevail. This means sovereignty, doesn't it? Ultimately, the decision is ours, not yours outside. It also states that any other law is invalid. What is the topic of discussion? Why should we compromise? I don't understand why we are giving in. Constitution, let me explain to you why this is dangerous, okay? Because if you violate it, regardless of your position, we can accuse you of treason. Yes, that's a big word.

But you are violating your country's constitution. This is not a personal matter. I am not speaking to any government. Please don't mix things up. I am not speaking to any government. I am talking about our constitution and the people's right to it. We are an independent state. Now, look at this statement. No government is more powerful than constitutional law. Isn't that so? Please write this down. Please get this CD. No government is more powerful than the constitution. Number two.

There is no government for the law to serve. The government is a servant of constitutional law. As you know, some people believe that they will live forever. I thank God for death, as you know. Death, I love death. Death, you are a blessing. Because death will eventually get rid of everything that is not working. You all better thank God that eternal life is not on Earth. As you know, some people only stay the same for a short time. This moves them, then they leave again. You are not above the constitution.

Third, the government is obligated to submit to, serve, and obey the constitution. The government is obligated to obey the constitution. Obligatory. This means that if they do not obey the constitution, they must be dismissed. This is correct. We employ governments to implement our constitutional aspirations. This is what we employ. Governments work for you. You employ her and she is obligated to achieve and implement the constitutional aspirations and values ​​of the people. It's not complicated.

So, first you need to know the constitution. So that you can learn how to judge the person you have hired. So, when you conduct an employee performance evaluation, yes, you will say that you fell short in this aspect, and therefore you will be dismissed. That's it. Or you do your job well, and you will be hired again. You can stay in your job. It depends on the circumstances. It's simple. Fourth, when the government violates constitutional law, this is considered high treason.

This means she is betraying the people. Take a deep breath. Do you know what the punishment for high treason is? In all countries? Execution. Now, I don't want anyone to write in a newspaper that I am calling for people to be executed. Good? I am simply explaining the basic principles to you. When the people's trust in the homeland is violated, it is called high treason. It is the most serious crime in the country. That's why the people of Egypt revolted.

That is why they are rising up in Syria now, because the people have had enough. They say, "Do you know something? This constitution, this person, and this person is above the constitution. Therefore, we will overthrow him." They went down to the streets and sat down. They said, "We will not go to work. We will block the road. We will do nothing. Why? Because you were fired from your jobs but you do not want to leave them." I only heard yesterday that the President of Syria realized his mistake.

So, what he is doing now is planning to hold dialogues with the people. Let me tell you something. It's too late. It's too late. Let me tell you this. Do you remember Bay Street? Yes, you remember him, Mr. Representative. Do you remember when we were about to explode? Don't pretend now, because you know that Bahamians don't smile. As you know, we are very kind. We have a lot of patience. But tell me the truth. Everything has its limits. This is what is happening in these countries. We are not immune to that.

My job as a leader in this community is to inform you of your constitutional right on Independence Day, which we celebrate and thank God for. We have a sovereign state. They applauded enthusiastically. It's Independence Day. Look at point five. The primary responsibility of the government is to protect, respect, defend, preserve, and abide by the integrity of the constitution and the law. Every word is important. This is their responsibility. And when they act irresponsibly, what do I do? Oh my God, I'm so excited.

If they act irresponsibly, they should be summoned. It should be said: " Look, you are not protecting the Constitution and the law. The Constitution states that any law that conflicts with our constitutional law is invalid." You are acting irresponsibly because the law you accept is contradictory. The decision you agree to is contradictory. Even the blind feel the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. Good. This is inspiration. God is excited because the truth is resonating from north to south today. Good.

Let me wrap this up, and then I'll give you some guidance because we'll finish this in the next session. Write this down. Truly civilized nations are not ruled by governments, but by the law. Do you know that? The government does not govern the Bahamas, but rather manages its affairs. There is a difference. This means that the law is above the government.

Civil societies are based on the principle of the rule of law, and therefore the law is more important than the constitution itself, because the constitution is the law that comes first. When a law is enacted, the law then protects it. That's why you have the right to sue anyone. The law protects the constitution, and protects the promises, rights and privileges that were given to the people in the constitution.

Today I read to you some of the most important articles of the constitution, and we are supposed to have governments that protect it. They didn't tell you that, as you can see. Did you know that we studied in the Bahamas, and the teachers never asked us to read the constitution, nor did they encourage us to do so? never. Isn't that so? Isn't that right, my brother? Never, is that right? never.

Therefore, I publicly call upon the Minister of Education today to make reading the Constitution compulsory for all students, numbering 62,000, and for teachers to read it in every semester from age four to ten. Some of you here, in your fifties, didn't know what you just read. Listen, I encourage you to stop complaining and start working. That's all I do. You complain when you don't know what to do. But once you know what you're doing, you stop complaining. You are working. Look at item six.

The law protects the nation from extinction. As you know, if we do not abide by our constitution, we may be swallowed up like Europe was swallowed up. I have visited almost all the countries in Europe. When I went to Sweden once, I couldn't wait to leave. I went to Amsterdam, and I was speaking at a conference with the Chamber of Commerce. And I was there. The place was crowded. After that night ended, the host asked me: "Have you ever visited the Red Light District in Amsterdam?" I replied: "No."

He said, "Do you want to go?" I replied: "No." He said, "I'll take you anyway." So I said, "Yes." He took me to the heart of Europe.
